title: KEDA Redis scaler miscalibration after metric multiplexing change — cold-start storm and elevated tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-09 evening regional capacity bursters observed a rapid cascade of cold starts in the serving fleet for hosted inference. Root symptom was a rapid scale-down after short-lived high-concurrency spikes: KEDA's Redis-based scaler undercounted active work due to a recent change in the metric multiplexing logic. The miscalibration produced false negatives for scale-up and false positives for scale-down which allowed pods to terminate while traffic still had KV cache requirements, causing elevated tail latency and user errors. This ticket records the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and longer-term actions taken to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-09 18:12 UTC — Pager alert: latency SLO breaches across /v1/stream endpoints in us-west-2
2026-02-09 18:15 UTC — Ops runbook checked; autoscaler showed rapid scale-down events starting at 18:05 UTC
2026-02-09 18:22 UTC — Identified sequences of short-lived bursts (avg 8s) where queue_length metric sampled as low during evaluation windows
2026-02-09 18:35 UTC — Rolled back keda-custom-scaler change deployed in runtime-1.28-canary to previous implementation (hotfix) — immediate reduction in scale-downs observed
2026-02-09 19:10 UTC — Enabled conservative cooldown and increased minReplicas for affected host pool; incident declared resolved at 19:45 UTC
2026-02-10 — Post-incident debugging: reproduced behavior locally with synthetic short-lived spike pattern and validated aggregator bug in multiplexing logic
2026-02-12 — Patch PR merged to change aggregator from mean to window-max and add sampling TTL guard (PR #12034)
2026-02-15 — Canary rollout of runtime-1.29 with patched scaler and telemetry dashboards; no regression during 72h window
impact_summary: Approximately 6% of user requests to hosted API in us-west-2 experienced >3x latency and ~0.5% increased error rate during the 90-minute event window. Internal dashboards show a measurable increase in cold start duration (median cold-start 420ms -> 1.6s). High-cost impact for customers with strict tail latency SLAs; several on-call pages and customer Slack mentions received.
root_cause: A change to the KEDA Redis scaler's metric multiplexing for improved efficiency introduced an aggregator that returned the average of sampled shard counters over the evaluation window. For our workload of many short-lived spikes, averaging masked transient peaks. Combined with a short scale-down cooldown (30s) and aggressive minReplicas=1, the autoscaler allowed scale-down during transient low samples. The immediate trigger was a canary deploy of the new aggregator in runtime-1.28 which removed a previous 'window-max' aggregation behavior.
immediate_mitigations: Rolled back the multiplexing change to the previous aggregator implementation (hotfix deployed 2026-02-09 18:35 UTC)
Temporarily increased minReplicas from 1 to 3 for affected serving pool
Increased scale-down cooldown to 180s for KEDA scaler policies in us-west-2
Enabled synthetic warmup traffic for new pods for 60s to prepopulate KV caches
Added a temporary alert for >3 scale-down events in 5m per pool
long_term_action_items: Change KEDA Redis scaler aggregator from mean to window-max with configurable percentile option (PR #12034) — merged and included in runtime-1.29
Introduce percentile smoothing (e.g., 95th over 2m) as a selectable aggregation mode for bursty workloads
Add per-pool warm-pool support (keep N idle replicas ready) and an operator flag to enable warm pools for low-latency customers (ENG-708000)
Increase default scale-down cooldown to 120s and add jitter to scale-down evaluation to avoid synchronized terminations
Add a unit/integration test harness that replays short-lived spike patterns against scaler logic and runs on PRs that touch scaler code
Expand observability: new dashboards for sample-level distribution of Redis counters, and a rate-of-change alert
Update runbook and playbook with clear rollback steps for scaler changes and an incident checklist for cold-start storms
followups: ENG-708000 — Warm pool operator and config flags design
ENG-709211 — Autoscaler test harness and CI gating
ENG-710101 — Update runbooks and on-call run-through session
ENG-711500 — Backfill historical metrics for 2025-12..2026-02 to evaluate incidence of short-lived spikes
notes: Engineering review: change was reviewed for performance but missed workload-pattern regression testing; emphasis added to PR checklist
PM note: recommend communication to top-10 customers in affected region summarizing root cause and mitigations
Design note: consider exposing a 'burst-friendly' autoscaling profile in Console that preconfigures percentile aggregation and warm-pool
communication: 2026-02-10 — Customer-facing summary drafted for top customers; sent to sales/AMs for review
2026-02-12 — Internal all-hands post-incident summary and Q&A held; recording stored in Confluence page
